# menu.List: Right and Left no longer walk the submenu cascade

## Context

Operator (2026-09-16): keyboard navigation through nested menus in `examples/button/base` once worked — arrows plus Space/Enter walked the cascade — and regressed when `main.addon.Navigator` arrived (#5123). The operator also ruled the pre-Navigator model out as the target: it selected on navigate and had no focus state. Focus as the cursor, with Space/Enter as the explicit select, is the intended UX.

Observed on `dev@d688710175`, `examples/button/base`, in-app browser with CDP key events. Each step starts from the previous one:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Click `Hello World` | Menu shows, focus on `Item 1` |
| ArrowDown ×2 | Focus on `Item 3` (a parent), nothing shown — correct under the focus model |
| ArrowRight on `Item 3` | **nothing** |
| Enter on `Item 3` | Submenu shows, focus moves to `Item 4` |
| ArrowDown | Focus on `Item 5` |
| ArrowLeft on `Item 5` | **nothing**: submenu stays, focus stays inside it |

## The Problem

#5123 (2023-12-22) moved arrow navigation out of `selection.ListModel#onNavKey`, which selected the next item, into the Navigator, which moves focus. It left `onKeyDown{Up,Down,Enter,Left,Right}` as placeholders. `selection.menu.ListModel` still assumes selection is the cursor:

- `onKeyDownRight()` calls `view.activeSubMenu?.selectionModel.selectAt(0)`. A focused parent has no active submenu, so Right is a no-op. When one is showing, Right moves that submenu's *selection*, not focus.
- `onKeyDownLeft()` re-selects `parentMenu`'s item at `parentIndex`. It is already selected, so nothing changes: the submenu is never hidden and focus never moves.
- **Space:** the Navigator activates on Enter only (`case 'Enter'` in its keydown handler), and no menu binds Space. This is a code reading, not yet run: the in-app browser's key instrument sends no key value for Space.

Enter works through a side effect: the Navigator clicks the item, selection shows the submenu, and `component.Base#afterSetMounted` focuses a floating component's first focusable child on mount.

## The Fix — `src/selection/menu/ListModel.mjs`, `src/menu/List.mjs`

Inside the focus model (arrows move focus; Enter, Space and click select and activate):

- **Right** on a focused parent shows its submenu and focuses the submenu's first item, including when the submenu is already showing. On a leaf: nothing.
- **Left** in a submenu hides it and focuses its parent item. In the root: nothing.
- **Escape** in a submenu hides that level and focuses its parent item. In the root: today's dismissal.
- **Space** on a focused item does what Enter does. The binding is menu-local; the Navigator stays unchanged for every other list.
- **Up/Down** stay focus-only: arrowing onto a parent shows nothing.

The focused item comes from the view's focus state (`list.Base#focusIndex`, which `onListNavigate()` already keeps current), never from selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Right on a focused parent shows its submenu and focuses its first item; Right on a leaf changes nothing (component spec, real keyboard).
- [ ] AC-2 Left in a submenu hides it and focuses the parent item; Left in the root changes nothing.
- [ ] AC-3 Escape in a submenu hides only that level and focuses the parent item.
- [ ] AC-4 Space on a parent behaves like Enter (shows its submenu, focus moves in); Space on a leaf runs its handler and dismisses like Enter.
- [ ] AC-5 Up/Down onto a parent show nothing.
- [ ] AC-6 A depth-2 walk by keyboard alone — `Item 3` → `Item 6` → `Item 7`, then back up to `Item 3` — with focus on the expected item at every step.
- [ ] AC-7 Existing menu unit and component specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Reintroducing selection on navigate (operator ruling above).
- Pointer hover — #18759.
- Changing the Navigator's key handling for other lists.

## Follow-up — focus-rest preview (operator direction, 2026-09-16)

Keyboard focus resting on a parent would show its submenu the way a pointer rest does (#18759), and Up/Down off it would hide it again; Right then only moves focus into what is already showing. It needs #18759's non-focusing preview show — without it, the mount-focus above pulls the cursor into every previewed submenu — and it changes this ticket's Left to "focus the parent, keep its submenu showing". **File when this ticket and #18759 have both merged.**

- 2026-09-16T11:58:14Z @tobiu referenced in commit `08f9d60` - "feat(menu): focus rests like a pointer rests (#18780) (#18783)

A pointer resting on a parent item previewed its submenu; the keyboard did neither half. Arrowing
onto a parent showed nothing, and arrowing OFF a parent left the submenu a hover had opened standing
under an item that no longer had focus.

Both come from one signal. `manager.Focus` fires `onFocusMove` on the closest component the old and
new focus paths share, which for an item-to-item move is the menu itself — so the menu now rests on
the item focus landed on, through the same timer, the same `showSubMenuOnHover` switch and the same
non-focusing `showSubMenu()` the pointer uses. One list resting on a new item drops what the previous
one showed, so the stale submenu closes without a rule of its own.

The case that needs no guard is the one a plausible implementation gets wrong: `ArrowRight` moving
focus INTO the submenu shares an ancestor of both menus, not this menu, so it never reaches
`onFocusMove` and the submenu it just opened stays open. A rule keyed on `onFocusLeave` would close
it — measured, and its CONTROL arm is the only one that reds under that mutation.

`Down onto a parent shows nothing` was asserted by a keyboard-cascade arm from #18760. That is the
behaviour this ticket reverses, so the arm now covers `Right on a leaf` and `Left in the root`, and
the focus-rest describe owns what Down does.

component.Base's onFocusMove docblock named `opts.newPath`; manager.Focus passes `path` and `oldPath`
plus the component. Corrected while relying on it — this is the hook's first implementer."
